### Observed differences

- Two segments exchanged their place in the flow. In the earlier window, the alternatives A19, A21 and A24 — about one of them ran per case (in roughly 30, 35 and 37 of 100 cases) — sat early in each case (mean relative event position about 0.34–0.36), while A20, A22 and A23, which ran in every case, sat late (about 0.63–0.64). In the later window, A20, A22 and A23 sit early (about 0.38) and A19, A21 and A24 sit late (about 0.66–0.68). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- All 21 tested activity pairs spanning the two segments reversed their order, most almost completely: A25 preceded A20 in about 99 of 100 cases before and followed it in about 99 of 100 after; A29 preceded A20 before and follows it now (about 98–99 of 100); A19 preceded A29 in the 30 of 100 cases containing both before and now follows it in 33 of 100. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021]
- The entry points into the segments swapped: outgoing transitions of A29 led to A20, A23 and A22 (about 37, 33 and 30 in 100) and now lead to A24, A19 and A21 (about 38, 32 and 29 in 100); outgoing transitions of A40 led to A24, A21 and A19 (about 34, 33 and 28 in 100) and now lead to A22, A20 and A23 (about 35, 31 and 28 in 100). [DIR007, DIR008]
- The exits swapped accordingly: A19, A21 and A24 led almost exclusively to A25 before (about 97–98 in 100 of their outgoing transitions) and lead to A30 now (about 95–98 in 100); A20, A22 and A23 led to A30 in about 29–37 in 100 before and lead to A25 in about 27–37 in 100 now, while their transitions among themselves stayed similar. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]
- Step distances match this rewiring: A29 reached A30 four steps later in about 93 of 100 observations before and two steps later in about 98 of 100 after; A40 reached A25 two steps later before (about 95 of 100) and four steps later after (about 92 of 100). The direct steps A21→A25 and A24→A25 (69–71 observations) are nearly gone (1–2 observations), A29 now reaches A21 in one step in 58 cases where the pair was previously seen within five steps only once, and A40 now reaches A20, A22 and A23 within one to three steps in essentially every case instead of in about one. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009]
- Participation and repetition barely moved: A20, A22, A23, A25 and A29 appear in every case in both windows, and about one of A19/A21/A24 per case with similar shares (about 33/29/40 in 100 now versus 30/35/37 before); A25 and A29 kept their middle positions, shifting only slightly later (mean position about 0.38→0.45 and 0.57→0.64). The difference is therefore where the segments sit in the flow, not how often they run. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that two segments exchanged places in the flow. In the earlier window, the flow ran from A29 into the segment A20–A22–A23 (all three, in varying order), which exited to A30, and from A40 into a choice of exactly one of A19, A21 and A24, which exited to A25. In the later window, A29 leads into the A19/A21/A24 choice, which exits to A30, and A40 leads into the A20–A22–A23 segment, which exits to A25, with A25 and A29 remaining between the two segments. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, LAG005, LAG009]

The reversal is shown directly and consistently: every cross-segment pair flipped its order, the successor profiles of both connector activities and all six segment activities changed exactly as the exchange predicts, positions moved by roughly a third of the case, and the adjacency changes match. Participation and repetition stayed the same, so this is a change in ordering and placement rather than a change in how often existing paths are taken. With 46 qualifying items against roughly 0.5 expected without a change in the control-flow family, chance sampling cannot account for the pattern, and a wholesale reversal of the flow direction is contradicted by the connector profiles (A29 now feeds the choice segment, not A25). [REL008, REL015, REL018, REL020, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, DIR007, DIR008, LAG001, LAG004, LAG005, LAG009]

Limitations: the evidence covers only the units that passed screening, so accompanying changes at unobserved activities between the segments (for example between A30 and A40, or between A25 and A29) cannot be excluded; and the data cannot distinguish a relocation of the two segments as blocks from an equivalent rewiring of the four connection points (A29's and A40's outputs and the segments' exits) — behaviourally the two descriptions coincide. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008]
